examples.ko: 동생이 제가 몰래 과자를 먹었다고 고자질했어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling told on me for secretly eating snacks.
A friend tattled to the teacher, so I got scolded.
Don't snitch; I'll tell them myself.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 다른 친구들 잘못을 자주 고자질해요.
examples.en: That child often tattles on other kids' mistakes.
I still don't know who snitched.
I'm worried my older brother will tell on me to Dad.

explain: '누구에게 고자질하다'처럼 '한테/에게/께'와 함께 써요. 비슷한 말로 '일러바치다'가 있는데 아이들 말에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling told Mom my secret.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고자질하다'와 뜻이 같고, 아이들 말에서 더 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same as '고자질하다' and is heard more often in children's speech.

phrases.example: 저는 친구에게 "선생님께 고자질하지 마" 하고 부탁했어요.
phrases.en: I asked my friend, "Don't snitch to the teacher."
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 마'는 반말로 친구에게 부탁하거나 말릴 때 써요. 존댓말은 '고자질하지 마세요'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-지 마' is the casual form for telling a friend not to do something. The polite form is '고자질하지 마세요'.

phrases.example: 고자질하는 친구와는 비밀 이야기를 하기 어려워요.
phrases.en: It's hard to share secrets with a friend who snitches.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 고자질을 잘하는 사람을 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-는' lets you describe a person who tends to snitch.

explain_en: It takes '한테', '에게' or '께' for the person told, as in '누구에게 고자질하다'. A similar word is '일러바치다', often heard in kids' speech.

examples.en: That puppy is the troublemaker of our house.

examples.ko: 쓰레기 문제가 이 동네의 골칫덩이가 됐어요.
examples.en: The trash problem has become this neighborhood's headache.
I finally replaced my pain-in-the-neck computer.

examples.ko: 처음엔 골칫덩이였는데 지금은 우리 팀의 에이스예요.
examples.en: He was a nuisance at first, but now he's our team's ace.

examples.ko: 주차 문제는 골칫덩이라서 아무도 손대려 하지 않아요.
examples.en: The parking issue is such a headache that nobody wants to touch it.
Please don't treat me like a nuisance.

explain: '골치 아프다'와 짝이 되는 말로, 골치 아프게 만드는 사람, 물건, 일에 모두 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 꽤 거친 말이라서 가까운 사이에서 농담처럼 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: Parking is a headache for our apartment complex.
phrases.nuance_ko: '골칫덩이'와 비슷하지만 사람보다 일이나 문제에 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '골칫덩이', but used more for problems than for people.

phrases.example: 그 오래된 차가 이제는 우리 집 골칫덩이가 됐어요.
phrases.en: That old car has become a nuisance for our family now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '되다'와 함께 써서 어떤 것이 문제를 일으키는 존재가 됐다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '되다' to say that something has turned into a source of trouble.

phrases.en: That cat is a nuisance to the neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: '골칫덩이'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same as '골칫덩이'.

explain_en: It pairs with '골치 아프다' (to be a headache) and can be used for people, things or problems that cause one. Said about a person it is quite harsh, so it is mostly used jokingly between close people.

en: to be hard on; to ill-treat; to molest

examples.ko: 시어머니가 며느리를 구박한다는 이야기는 드라마에 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Stories of a mother-in-law mistreating her daughter-in-law often appear in dramas.
If a senior is hard on a newcomer, the atmosphere gets bad.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 형이 저를 많이 구박했어요.
examples.en: When we were young, my older brother was often hard on me.

examples.ko: 동생을 구박하지 말고 잘 챙겨 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't be harsh to your younger sibling; take good care of them.

examples.ko: 그렇게 구박해도 그 친구는 웃기만 했어요.
examples.en: Even when I was that harsh to him, that friend just laughed.

examples.ko: 구박하는 말투 때문에 사람들이 그를 피해요.
examples.en: People avoid him because of his belittling way of speaking.

explain: 약한 사람을 계속 못마땅해하며 못살게 구는 것이에요. '괴롭히다'보다 말과 태도로 눈치를 주거나 홀대한다는 느낌이 강하고, 영어의 'molest'처럼 성적인 뜻은 없어요. '구박을 받다'라고도 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: I heard that as a child, she was mistreated by her stepmother.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구박하다'의 당하는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person being mistreated.

phrases.en: I felt sorry for the new employee who was being picked on at work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구박을 받다'와 뜻이 같고, 조금 더 짧게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 구박을 받다, just shorter.

phrases.en: You shouldn't make your friend's life miserable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 많이 쓰는 말로, 계속 괴롭힌다는 느낌이 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common everyday phrase with a clear sense of continuous harassment.

explain_en: It means continually treating a weaker person with disapproval and making their life hard. Compared with '괴롭히다', it focuses on words and attitude, such as cold treatment or belittling, and it has no sexual meaning like the English 'molest'. People often say '구박을 받다' too.

examples.en: The child whispered a secret in her mom's ear.
Even whispering in the theater is surprisingly loud.
My friend whispered right into my ear.

examples.ko: 회의 중에는 옆 사람에게 귓속말하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't whisper to the person next to you during the meeting.
What are you two whispering about like that?
I heard all of their whispering.

explain: '속삭이다'는 작은 소리로 말하는 것이고, 귓속말하다는 남이 못 듣게 상대 귀에 가까이 대고 말하는 거예요. '귓속말을 하다', '귓속말을 주고받다'처럼도 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 친구가 제 귀에 대고 귓속말을 했어요.
phrases.en: My friend whispered in my ear.
phrases.nuance_ko: '귓속말하다'를 '목적어 + 하다' 형태로 풀어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same verb split into 'object + 하다'.

phrases.en: The two of them keep whispering to each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 비밀스럽게 이야기를 나눌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when two people share secret talk with each other.

phrases.en: The child whispered into her mom's ear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 소리로 말하는 것이라 귓속말하다보다 뜻이 조금 넓어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means speaking softly, so it is a bit broader than 귓속말하다.

explain_en: '속삭이다' means to speak in a low voice, while 귓속말하다 means putting your mouth near someone's ear so others can't hear. It's also common as '귓속말을 하다' or '귓속말을 주고받다'.

examples.ko: 남을 깎아내려서 자기가 높아지는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Putting others down doesn't make you any higher.
He tends to belittle his colleagues' achievements.
Please don't belittle my efforts.

examples.ko: 경쟁 상대를 깎아내리는 광고는 좋지 않아요.
examples.en: Ads that run down the competition are not good.
I didn't say it on purpose to put you down.

examples.ko: 사람들이 그 작품을 깎아내렸지만 저는 좋아요.
examples.en: People disparaged the work, but I like it.

explain: 다른 사람이나 그의 가치, 평판을 실제보다 낮게 말할 때 써요. 반대는 '치켜세우다'나 '띄워 주다'예요. '헐뜯다'는 더 직접적으로 흉을 보는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Don't belittle other people's effort.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그러지 말라고 부탁하거나 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask or tell someone not to do this.

phrases.en: I feel bad when I hear belittling words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남을 낮추어 말하는 말을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to words that put someone down.

phrases.example: 그 기자는 상대 선수의 실력을 깎아내렸어요.
phrases.en: That reporter downplayed the other player's skill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 일어난 일을 말하는 해요체 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite past form for something that already happened.

explain_en: It is used when you speak of a person, or their value or reputation, as lower than it really is. The opposites are '치켜세우다' and '띄워 주다'. '헐뜯다' feels more like directly badmouthing someone.

examples.en: Anglers are gathered by the lake.
My father is a well-known angler.
The angler caught a big fish.

examples.ko: 새벽부터 낚시꾼 몇 명이 강가에 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: A few anglers have been sitting by the river since dawn.
It is a popular spot for anglers.

examples.ko: 저 낚시꾼은 하루 종일 한 마리도 못 잡았어요.
examples.en: That angler didn't catch a single fish all day.

explain: '-꾼'은 어떤 일을 자주 하거나 잘하는 사람에게 붙어요. 낚시를 즐기는 사람을 말할 때 '낚시꾼'이라고 해요. 가볍게 한 번 해 본 사람은 '낚시하는 사람'이라고 말하는 편이 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: There are many anglers on the bridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들'을 붙여 여러 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 들 makes it plural.

phrases.en: I saw a person fishing by the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낚시꾼'보다 가볍게 한 번 하는 사람도 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also covers someone who fishes only casually.

phrases.en: My father became an angler after retiring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낚시를 자주 즐기는 사람이 된다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says someone has become a regular angler.

explain_en: '-꾼' is added to someone who does something often or is good at it. '낚시꾼' is someone who really enjoys fishing. For someone who just tried it once, '낚시하는 사람' sounds more natural.

examples.ko: 내숭 떨지 말고 그냥 배고프다고 말해요.
examples.en: Stop playing coy and just say you're hungry.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 처음 만난 사람 앞에서는 내숭을 떨어요.
examples.en: That friend acts coy in front of people they've just met.
They're so coy that it's hard to know what they really think.

examples.ko: 이제 내숭 그만 떨고 편하게 먹어요.
examples.en: Stop being coy now and eat comfortably.

examples.ko: 겉으로는 착해 보여도 알고 보면 내숭 덩어리예요.
examples.en: They look nice on the surface, but actually they're full of pretense.

examples.ko: 너 사실은 말 많은 거 알아, 내숭 부리지 마요.
examples.en: I know you actually talk a lot, so don't act coy.

explain: '내숭을 떨다', '내숭을 부리다'로 자주 말해요. 얌전하거나 모르는 척하며 속마음을 감추는 모습인데, 친한 사이에서 놀리듯 말하는 경우가 많아서 어른께는 조심해서 써야 해요.

phrases.example: 좋아하면서 왜 싫은 척 내숭을 떨어요?
phrases.en: Why are you acting coy when you actually like it?
phrases.nuance_ko: '내숭'을 가장 자연스럽게 쓰는 짝말로, 속마음을 감추고 얌전한 척하는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural collocation for 내숭; it means hiding your true feelings and acting demure.

phrases.en: My younger sibling only acts coy in front of guests.
phrases.nuance_ko: '내숭을 떨다'와 뜻이 같고, 둘 다 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '내숭을 떨다'; both are common.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 내숭이 심해서 속마음을 몰라요.
phrases.en: That friend is so coy that I can't tell what they really think.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성격이나 태도를 평가할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe or judge someone's personality or attitude.

explain_en: It is often said as '내숭을 떨다' or '내숭을 부리다'. It describes acting demure or innocent while hiding one's real nature. It is mostly used to tease close friends, so be careful using it with elders.

examples.ko: 저는 걸음이 느려서 친구들이 느림보라고 불러요.
examples.en: I walk slowly, so my friends call me a slowpoke.
The tortoise is famous for being slow.

examples.ko: 저 느림보 좀 보세요, 아직도 신발을 신고 있어요.
examples.en: Look at that slowpoke, still putting on his shoes.

examples.ko: 동생은 밥 먹을 때 느림보가 돼요.
examples.en: My sibling turns into a slowpoke when eating.
I took a super slow bus and was late for the appointment.
My son is like a slowpoke every morning.

explain: 행동이 느린 사람이나 동물을 가볍게 놀릴 때 써요. 친한 사이에는 장난스럽게 쓰지만, 모르는 사람에게 하면 실례일 수 있어요. 비슷한 말로 '굼벵이', 반대로 '날쌘돌이'가 있어요.

phrases.en: I'm a slowpoke in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '느림보'와 비슷하게 행동이 느린 사람을 놀리는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 느림보, a teasing word for a slow person.

phrases.en: The slowpoke turtle walks slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물 이야기나 동화에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing that often appears in animal stories and fairy tales.

phrases.example: 달리기를 할 때 저는 느림보 같아요.
phrases.en: When I run, I feel like a slowpoke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 자신이 느리다고 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say lightly that you yourself are slow.

explain_en: It lightly teases a slow person or animal. Among close people it sounds playful, but saying it to a stranger can be rude. A similar word is '굼벵이', and an opposite is '날쌘돌이'.

en: to be modest; to be gentle

examples.ko: 다소곳한 모습으로 앉아 있는 아이가 귀여워요.
examples.en: The child sitting so demurely is cute.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말투가 다소곳해서 호감이 가요.
examples.en: She speaks so gently that I like her.
In front of elders, you should behave modestly.
She looks meek, but she is strong inside.
Her bowed head looked so demure.
The child who had been so quiet suddenly laughed loudly.

explain: '얌전하다'와 비슷하지만, 고개를 조금 숙이고 말없이 온순한 모습을 그릴 때 더 잘 어울려요. 씩씩하고 활발한 사람에게는 잘 쓰지 않고, 보통 태도나 모습을 칭찬하듯 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: Her gentle, modest manner is lovely to see.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 형태로, 모습을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifying form before a noun, used to praise someone's appearance.

phrases.en: That child looked demure at first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 얌전해 보인다는 느낌으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone looks gentle on the outside.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is well-behaved in front of guests.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 일상적이고 넓게 쓰이는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more everyday, broadly used similar word.

explain_en: It is close to '얌전하다', but fits best when picturing someone with a slightly lowered head and a quiet, gentle manner. It is rarely used for lively, energetic people and usually describes a manner or appearance in a complimentary way.

en: to be unyielding; to be powerful

examples.en: That child is tough and brave even though he's young.

examples.ko: 발표할 때 대찬 모습에 모두 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Everyone was surprised at how bold he looked during the presentation.

examples.ko: 선생님 앞에서도 대차게 자기 생각을 말했어요.
examples.en: She boldly said what she thought even in front of the teacher.

examples.ko: 그는 대차서 어떤 일에도 겁을 내지 않아요.
examples.en: He's gutsy, so he isn't afraid of anything.
She looks frail, but she's tough inside.
The new hire boldly stepped up to take on the task.

explain: 겁 없이 야무지고 배짱 있는 성격이나 태도를 칭찬할 때 써요. '당차다'와 비슷하고, 사람의 성격이나 말투, 행동에 잘 어울려요. '대찬 목소리'처럼 ㄴ이 붙어 '대찬'이 돼요.

phrases.en: He answered boldly in the interview.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사형이라 '말하다', '대답하다' 같은 동사 앞에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adverb form placed before verbs like speak or answer.

phrases.en: Our youngest is small but very gutsy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성격을 말하는 해요체 서술형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite predicate form describing someone's character.

phrases.en: That spirited kid is the class president.
phrases.nuance_ko: '당차다'는 '대차다'와 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 당차다 is a close synonym of 대차다.

explain_en: It praises a fearless, firm and gutsy personality or attitude. It is similar to '당차다' and suits a person's character, way of speaking or actions. The modifier form is '대찬', as in '대찬 목소리'.

examples.en: I am careless, so I often lose things.
My older sister is a scatterbrain, but she has a warm heart.

examples.ko: 덜렁이 동생이 또 우산을 두고 왔어요.
examples.en: My scatterbrained younger sibling left an umbrella behind again.

examples.ko: 덜렁이처럼 굴지 말고 한 번 더 확인하세요.
examples.en: Don't be careless, and check one more time.
My friends call me a scatterbrain.

examples.ko: 덜렁이인 남편 때문에 열쇠는 항상 제가 챙겨요.
examples.en: Because my husband is forgetful, I always keep the keys.

explain: 침착하지 못하고 자주 실수하거나 물건을 잘 잃어버리는 사람을 가볍게 놀리듯 부르는 말이에요. 친한 사이나 자기 자신에게 쓰면 괜찮지만, 처음 만난 사람이나 어른에게는 조심하는 게 좋아요. '덜렁대다'처럼 동사로도 말해요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is often careless and makes mistakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아니라 행동을 말하는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb describing the behavior rather than the person.

phrases.example: 제가 오늘도 우산을 놓고 왔어요. 덜렁이 같죠?
phrases.en: I left my umbrella behind again today. I'm such a scatterbrain, right?
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 자신에게 가볍게 쓰기 좋은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light way to describe yourself.

phrases.en: My scatterbrained friend lost their wallet again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친한 사이에서 가볍게 놀리듯 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used playfully between close friends.

explain_en: It teases someone who is hasty, makes mistakes often or loses things. It is fine with close friends or about yourself, but be careful with strangers or elders. The verb form '덜렁대다' is also used.

en: to be indifferent; to be unfriendly

examples.en: I'm still a bit distant with my cousin since we met after a long time.

examples.ko: 동료와 싸운 뒤로 서로 데면데면하게 지내요.
examples.en: Since the fight with my coworker, we've been cool toward each other.
I'm shy with strangers, so I tend to be distant at first.
Why are you so cold to me these days?
We used to be distant, but we got closer after the trip.
We're siblings, but we're so distant with each other that it feels awkward.

explain: '서먹서먹하다'와 가깝지만, 데면데면하다는 태도가 살갑지 않고 무덤덤한 쪽에 가까워요. 친해질 만한 사이인데 정이 없어 보일 때 많이 써요. 반대로 따뜻하고 가까운 느낌은 '살갑다'로 말해요.

phrases.example: 동창을 오랜만에 만나서 아직 좀 데면데면해요.
phrases.en: I haven't seen my old classmate in a while, so we're still a bit distant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어를 해요체로 말한 형태로, 지금 사이가 무덤덤하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the polite present form, used to say the relationship is currently cold or distant.

phrases.en: Even though we're family, we're not close.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 명사 '사이'를 꾸며서 두 사람의 관계를 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describes a relationship with the noun '사이'.

phrases.en: He treated the new coworker coldly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람을 대하는 태도가 살갑지 않을 때 쓰는 부사형 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form describes an unfriendly attitude toward someone.

explain_en: It is close to '서먹서먹하다', but 데면데면하다 leans toward a cold, unaffectionate attitude. It is often used when two people could be close but seem to have no warmth. The opposite, warm and friendly, is '살갑다'.

examples.en: I got angry because my younger brother hogged the game console.

examples.ko: 한 사람이 인기를 독차지하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: One person shouldn't take all the popularity.
My older brother took the whole sofa for himself.

examples.ko: 그 영화가 올해 상을 독차지할 거예요.
examples.en: That movie will sweep the awards this year.
There were no customers, so I sat with the whole shop to myself.
Please don't dominate the conversation by yourself.

explain: '혼자 차지하다'와 비슷하지만 '독차지하다'에는 남이 나눠 가져야 할 몫까지 혼자 갖는다는 불만의 느낌이 있어요. 사랑, 인기, 상, 자리처럼 나눌 수 있는 것에 자주 써요.

phrases.en: That actor monopolized popularity this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들의 관심이 한 사람에게만 모였을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when everyone's attention gathers on just one person.

phrases.en: My older brother took the whole room for himself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로 이미 혼자 가졌다는 불만을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, used to complain that someone already took it all.

phrases.en: Please don't take all the good seats for yourself.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혼자 다 가지지 말고 나누라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone not to keep it all and to share.

explain_en: It is close to '혼자 차지하다' (take for oneself), but '독차지하다' carries a note of complaint that someone is taking a share meant for others. It often goes with love, popularity, prizes and seats.

examples.ko: 우리 반에는 동명이인이 두 명 있어요.
examples.en: There are two people with the same name in our class.
We have the same name, so the email went to the wrong person.

examples.ko: 저와 이름이 같은 동명이인을 처음 만났어요.
examples.en: I met someone with the same name as me for the first time.
There are quite a few people with the same names at this school.

examples.ko: 뉴스에 나온 사람은 제 친구와 동명이인이에요.
examples.en: The person in the news just has the same name as my friend.

examples.ko: 동명이인끼리 이름표가 바뀌는 일이 가끔 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes people with the same name get their name tags mixed up.

explain: 이름만 같고 서로 다른 사람을 말해요. '뉴스에 나온 사람은 동명이인이에요'처럼 같은 사람이 아니라는 걸 분명히 할 때 자주 써요.

phrases.en: That actor and I have the same name but are different people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'A와 B는 동명이인이다'처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as 'A and B are dongmyeongiin'.

phrases.en: I got confused because of someone with the same name.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름이 같아서 생긴 문제를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For problems caused by sharing a name.

phrases.en: I met someone with my name at school for the first time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나와 이름이 같은 사람을 만났을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For meeting a person who shares your name.

explain_en: It refers to different people who happen to share the same name. It is often used to make clear that it's not the same person, as in '뉴스에 나온 사람은 동명이인이에요'.

examples.ko: 험담을 들어도 맞장구치지 않고 화제를 바꿨어요.
examples.en: Even when I heard gossip, I didn't chime in and changed the subject.

examples.ko: 친구가 이야기할 때 맞장구치면 대화가 즐거워져요.
examples.en: If you chime in while a friend is talking, the conversation gets more fun.
I agreed without thinking and got into an awkward situation.

examples.ko: 동생이 제 말마다 맞장구쳐 줘서 신나게 이야기했어요.
examples.en: My sibling chimed in on everything I said, so I talked happily.

examples.ko: 저는 그 사람 의견에 맞장구칠 수가 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't go along with that person's opinion.

examples.ko: 맞장구치는 소리가 들리니까 잘 듣고 있다는 게 느껴져요.
examples.en: Hearing you chime in, I can tell you're listening well.

explain: '동의하다'는 딱딱한 말이고, '맞장구치다'는 '맞아요, 그렇죠' 같은 말이나 끄덕임으로 상대 말에 호응하는 대화체예요. 속으로는 동의하지 않아도 분위기를 맞추려고 할 때도 쓰고, '맞장구를 치다'로 띄어 써도 돼요.

phrases.en: I chimed in agreeing with my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맞장구치다'를 띄어 쓴 형태로, 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced form of 'majjangguchida', with the same meaning.

phrases.en: My mom nodded along to what I said.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대를 위해 호응해 주는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the feeling of responding in agreement for the other person's sake.

phrases.en: I agree with that opinion too.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맞장구치다'보다 딱딱하고 회의나 글에도 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: More formal than 'majjangguchida'; fits meetings and writing.

explain_en: '동의하다' is stiff, while '맞장구치다' is conversational, meaning to respond to the other person with words like '맞아요' or a nod. It can be used even when you don't truly agree but go along to keep the mood, and it can also be written '맞장구를 치다'.

en: to lash out; to rebuke strongly

examples.en: The team leader kept berating the junior who made a mistake.

examples.ko: 그렇게 몰아세우면 아이가 더 주눅 들어요.
examples.en: If you pressure the child like that, he'll become even more intimidated.
I'm sorry for pressing my friend as if he were the culprit.

examples.ko: 저를 몰아세우지 말고 천천히 물어봐 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't attack me, and ask slowly.

examples.ko: 모두가 한 사람만 몰아세우는 분위기가 싫었어요.
examples.en: I disliked the atmosphere where everyone piled on one person.

examples.ko: 저를 죄인처럼 몰아세우듯 말하지 말고 부드럽게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't talk to me as if you were cornering a criminal; speak gently.

explain: 상대의 잘못을 말로 계속 심하게 따지고 나무랄 때 써요. '야단치다'보다 몰아붙이고 추궁하는 느낌이 강하고, '~을/를 몰아세우다' 모양으로 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '몰아붙이다'도 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: Please don't push him that hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몰아세우다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 일상에서 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 몰아세우다 and common in everyday speech.

phrases.example: 대답을 못 하자 선생님이 자꾸 다그쳤어요.
phrases.en: When I couldn't answer, the teacher kept pressing me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빨리 말하라고 몰아 묻는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has the feel of pressing someone to answer quickly.

phrases.en: Please don't scold the child like that.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그만하라고 부탁하는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask someone to stop.

explain_en: It means to keep criticizing and pressing someone hard over a fault with words. It feels more like cornering and interrogating than '야단치다' (to scold), and takes the pattern '~을/를 몰아세우다'. '몰아붙이다' is often used with a similar meaning.

examples.en: I know nothing about cooking.
Sorry, it's an uninformed question.

examples.ko: 그렇게 무식하게 힘으로만 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't just use brute force like that.
My friend teased me, saying I'm clueless.
I was ignorant, so I didn't even know this.

examples.ko: 무식했던 저는 책을 많이 읽기 시작했어요.
examples.en: I used to be ignorant, so I started reading many books.

explain: 사람에게 직접 쓰면 '배우지 못한 사람'이라는 무례한 말이 될 수 있어서, 남에게 하지 않는 게 좋아요. 자기 자신에게 겸손하게 쓰거나 '무식하게 힘만 쓰다'처럼 방법이 투박하다는 뜻으로 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 무식하게 힘만 쓰지 말고 요령을 배우세요.
phrases.en: Don't just use brute force; learn the trick.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙이면 방법이 투박하다는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -게, it means the way of doing something is crude.

phrases.en: It's a crude method, but it's sure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아니라 방법을 가리켜서 덜 무례해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes a method rather than a person, so it is less rude.

phrases.en: I don't know much about cooking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 자신에 대해 더 부드럽게 말하고 싶을 때 무식하다 대신 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer way to talk about yourself instead of 무식하다.

explain_en: Said directly to someone, it sounds rude, like calling them uneducated, so avoid using it about other people. Koreans use it humbly about themselves, or about a crude method, as in 무식하게 힘만 쓰다 (to rely on brute force).

en: to taunt; to be sarcastic; to sneer at

examples.ko: 친구가 내 실수를 보고 계속 비아냥거려요.
examples.en: My friend keeps sneering at me after seeing my mistake.

examples.ko: 비아냥거리는 말투 때문에 대화가 자꾸 싸움으로 끝나요.
examples.en: Because of the sarcastic tone, our conversations keep ending in fights.
Why do you talk in such a sarcastic way?

examples.ko: 동료가 내 발표를 비아냥거려서 기분이 상했어요.
examples.en: A coworker made snide remarks about my presentation, and it upset me.
He said 'You're really something' as if mocking me.

examples.ko: 선배가 비아냥거릴 때마다 저는 못 들은 척해요.
examples.en: Whenever my senior makes snide remarks, I pretend not to hear.

explain: '놀리다'는 장난일 수도 있지만 '비아냥거리다'는 상대를 깎아내리려고 비꼬는 기분 나쁜 말투예요. '비아냥대다'라고도 하고, 명사 '비아냥'은 '비아냥을 떨다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: He sneers at the end of every sentence, so it's uncomfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비아냥거리다'와 같은 뜻으로 일상에서 줄여서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '비아냥거리다'; commonly used in everyday speech.

phrases.en: He spoke sarcastically, so the mood turned bad.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'로 말하는 방식을 함께 나타낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-며' form shows how someone speaks at the same time.

phrases.example: 비아냥 섞인 말을 들으니 기분이 나빴어요.
phrases.en: I felt bad hearing those sarcastic words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '비아냥'에 '섞인'을 붙여 비꼬는 말투가 담긴 말을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun '비아냥' with '섞인' to refer to words with a sarcastic tone.

explain_en: '놀리다' (tease) can be playful, but '비아냥거리다' is sarcastic talk meant to put someone down and feels unpleasant. It is also said as '비아냥대다', and the noun '비아냥' is used as in '비아냥을 떨다'.

examples.ko: 서울에 처음 왔을 때 저는 시골뜨기 같았어요.
examples.en: When I first came to Seoul, I felt like a country bumpkin.
You shouldn't tease someone by calling them a bumpkin.
The main character in the movie was a simple country bumpkin.
He tried hard to lose his country-bumpkin look.

examples.ko: 도시 사람들이 나를 시골뜨기로 볼까 봐 걱정했어요.
examples.en: I worried that city people would see me as a hick.
I was upset because I was treated like a bumpkin for being unsophisticated.

explain: 세련되지 못한 시골 사람을 낮잡아 부르는 말이라 다른 사람에게 쓰면 실례예요. 주로 이야기 속 인물을 말하거나, 자신을 웃으며 낮출 때 써요. 비슷한 말로 '촌놈'이 있는데 이것도 거친 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 서울에 처음 왔을 때 저는 완전히 시골뜨기 같았어요.
phrases.en: When I first came to Seoul, I felt like a total country bumpkin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자신을 웃으며 낮출 때 쓰기 좋은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A good phrase for humorously putting yourself down.

phrases.en: I was upset about being treated like a hick in the city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이 무시하는 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when others look down on someone.

phrases.en: The protagonist of that novel is a naive country bumpkin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기 속 인물을 소개할 때 '순진한'과 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with 순진한 when introducing a character in a story.

explain_en: It is a belittling term for an unsophisticated country person, so using it about someone is rude. It mostly describes a character in a story or is used jokingly about oneself. A similar word is '촌놈', which also sounds rough.

en: to be absent-minded; to be dazed

examples.en: I'm new, so I'm still a bit lost.
Your bumbling look was cute.
I'm always out of it in the morning, so I make mistakes.
It was my first time there, so I felt lost.
Don't act so spaced out.
The newbie who used to be lost now does the work well.

explain: 신입이나 낯선 곳에서 정신이 없고 서툰 사람에게 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. 놀리는 느낌이 있을 수 있어서 윗사람에게는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.

phrases.en: He looks a bit scatterbrained, but he does his work well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 서툴러 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone appears clumsy or unprepared on the surface.

phrases.en: I'm reminded of when I was a bumbling newbie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸미는 형태로, 신입이나 초보와 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form, often used with words like newcomer or beginner.

phrases.en: I'm no longer flustered and I'm used to the work now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서툴던 때를 지나 익숙해졌다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you've gotten past the clumsy stage and are used to things.

explain_en: It is a casual word for someone who is flustered and clumsy, like a newcomer in an unfamiliar place. It can sound teasing, so avoid using it about people older or higher than you.

examples.en: The smell of cake is tempting me.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 좋은 조건으로 선수를 유혹했어요.
examples.en: That company lured the player with good terms.

examples.ko: 친구가 놀러 가자고 유혹해서 숙제를 못 했어요.
examples.en: My friend tempted me to go out, so I couldn't do my homework.
Ads have many ways to entice consumers.
Be careful when someone tries to lure you with sweet words.

examples.ko: 숲의 새소리가 나를 아침 산책으로 유혹했어요.
examples.en: The birdsong in the forest lured me out for a morning walk.

explain: 사람뿐 아니라 음식, 광고, 돈도 주어가 될 수 있어요. 명사 '유혹'과 함께 '유혹에 빠지다', '유혹을 이기다'처럼 자주 써요. 나쁜 일로 끌어들일 때뿐 아니라 맛있는 음식이 마음을 끌 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I fell into the temptation of sweet food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유혹을 이기지 못했다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often means failing to resist temptation.

phrases.en: I beat the temptation and exercised.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유혹에 빠지다'의 반대로, 참아 냈을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of falling into temptation; used when you hold out.

phrases.en: Please don't tempt me with ramen at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유혹하다'를 부정 명령형으로 말하는 존댓말 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite negative command form of 유혹하다.

explain_en: The subject can be a person, but also food, an ad, or money. The noun is common in '유혹에 빠지다' (fall into temptation) and '유혹을 이기다' (resist temptation). It covers pulling someone toward something bad, and also food that is hard to resist.

examples.ko: 둘이 또 사소한 일로 입씨름을 해요.
examples.en: Those two are bickering again over something small.

examples.ko: 입씨름 좀 그만하고 이제 밥 먹어요.
examples.en: Stop arguing and let's eat now.
If I argue with my brother, I lose anyway.

examples.ko: 입씨름 끝에 결국 제가 먼저 사과했어요.
examples.en: After the squabble, I ended up apologizing first.
As the meeting dragged on, it was nothing but wrangling.
It is better to avoid pointless arguments.

explain: 몸싸움이 아니라 말로만 티격태격하는 걸 말하고, 결론 없이 계속 따지는 느낌이 있어요. '말다툼'보다 가볍게 쓸 때가 많아요. '입씨름을 하다/벌이다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I had an argument with my younger sibling this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '입씨름'보다 조금 더 화가 난 싸움으로 들릴 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can sound like a slightly angrier fight than the headword.

phrases.en: The two of them squabbled for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한동안 말로 계속 다툰다는 뜻의 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing meaning to go back and forth verbally for a while.

phrases.en: Don't bicker over something so small.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '입씨름'에 '하다'를 붙여 행동으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, used to describe the act of bickering.

explain_en: It means a fight with words only, not fists, and it often feels like going back and forth with no conclusion. It is often a bit lighter than '말다툼'. Say '입씨름을 하다/벌이다'.

examples.ko: 우리 삼촌은 허풍쟁이라서 말을 반만 들어요.
examples.en: My uncle is a braggart, so I only half believe him.
He has a reputation as a braggart.
My braggart friend started showing off again.
Nobody wants to be a blowhard.
Everyone calls him a braggart.
Don't talk like a blowhard; just tell the facts.

explain: '-쟁이'가 붙어 그런 버릇이 있는 사람을 놀릴 때 쓰는 말이라서, 친한 사이가 아니면 직접 말하지 않는 게 좋아요. 비슷한 말로 '허풍선이'가 있어요. 없는 일을 지어내기보다 사실을 부풀려 말하는 사람에게 많이 써요.

phrases.en: He's a blowhard, so he's hard to trust.
phrases.nuance_ko: '허풍쟁이'와 거의 같은 뜻의 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A near-synonym of 허풍쟁이.

phrases.example: 허풍이 심한 사람이라 말을 다 믿지는 않아요.
phrases.en: He exaggerates a lot, so I don't believe everything he says.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀리는 느낌 없이 부드럽게 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gentler way to say it without teasing.
phrases.en_equiv: a person who exaggerates a lot

phrases.en: That friend seems like a braggart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그런 느낌이 든다고 조심스럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say cautiously that someone seems that way.

explain_en: Because '-쟁이' is used to tease someone with such a habit, it is better not to say it directly to anyone you're not close to. A similar word is '허풍선이'. It is often used for someone who inflates the facts rather than makes things up.

en: to be in harmony; to unite in harmony

examples.en: Our class gets along and helps each other.

examples.ko: 다른 나라 사람들과 화합하는 법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned how to live in harmony with people from other countries.
The sports day is a good chance for students to come together.

examples.ko: 두 가족이 화합하고 나서 분위기가 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: The mood improved after the two families came together.
Work goes well only when the staff are in harmony.

examples.ko: 회식은 팀이 화합할 수 있게 도와줘요.
examples.en: Company dinners help the team to bond.

explain: '화합하다'는 사람이나 집단이 다툼 없이 마음을 모을 때 써요. '단결하다'는 같은 목표로 뭉치는 느낌이 강하고, '화합하다'는 사이좋게 어울리는 느낌이 커요. 물건에는 쓰지 않고 사람에게만 써요.

phrases.en: The harmonious atmosphere in the meeting was nice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사이좋게 어울리는 분위기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes an atmosphere of getting along well.

phrases.en: The two teams came together in harmony and won.
phrases.nuance_ko: '화합하다'를 명사로 바꾼 말로 조금 딱딱해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun form, a bit more formal.

phrases.en: The two people could not get along for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사이좋게 지내지 못할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people cannot get along.

explain_en: '화합하다' is for people or groups joining hearts without conflict. '단결하다' stresses banding together for a goal, while '화합하다' stresses getting along. It is used for people, never things.
